## Verdict

The committed default-branch fleet closure criterion for v0.46 is met. All nine managed adopters have AWF 0.46.0 from release revision `d2924d068114` at schema 50 on `main`. Every AWF rollout commit changes exactly `.awf/awf.lock`, `.awf/bootstrap.sh`, and `docs/config-reference.md`, with no added or removed path. At each rollout tree, the managed path set matches its v0.45 baseline and every managed file other than bootstrap and config reference is byte-identical.

The follow-on adopter outcome recorded with the R0-R5 architecture milestone is closed. Seven repositories have successful exact-SHA hosted project checks. Pi Tools and Razer KB Manager have no project CI configured.

This report is settled closure evidence, not product policy, a release record, or a claim that every live machine and process is current.

## Method and common result

The census on 2026-09-01 used fresh authenticated GitHub repository, commit, Actions, check-run, and status queries plus a fresh shallow clone of every hosted default branch. For each repository, the GitHub API SHA, `git ls-remote` SHA, and cloned `main` SHA agreed. All nine rollout commits have valid GitHub signature verification. Independent adopter owners then revalidated canonical native gates and current hosted tips; the census refreshed every tip that advanced.

At every current remote tree:

- `.awf/awf.lock` records `awfVersion: 0.46.0` and `schemaVersion: 50`; invoking the pinned binary reports `version: 0.46.0 (rev d2924d068114)`.
- Fresh `./awf check` succeeds without changing the checkout.
- The original rollout commit has three modified paths and no additions or removals: `.awf/awf.lock`, `.awf/bootstrap.sh`, and `docs/config-reference.md`.
- At the rollout commit, the lock's managed path-key set is unchanged from the repository's v0.45 rollout tree. Across that set, only `.awf/bootstrap.sh` and `docs/config-reference.md` have changed bytes; all other managed bytes are identical.
- `.pi/extensions/awf-effort/client.ts`, `.pi/extensions/awf-effort/index.ts`, the repository-named Pi `using-effort` skill, and retired Pi activity or effort-memory protocol residue are absent.
- All eleven native skills are present, including `.pi/skills/<prefix>-effort-workflow/SKILL.md`. The effort workflow resolves memory through `./awf effort show <slug>` and uses ordinary file tools under the one-writer rule.
- `.pi/extensions/awf-subagents/index.ts`, `.pi/extensions/awf-subagents/model-routing.ts`, and the four native agent definitions are present. The adapter retains bounded model routing, protocol-v2 request, capability, receipt, and result handling, and the exact four tools `subagent_grounding`, `subagent_explore`, `subagent_review_code`, and `subagent_implement`.
- A read-only `./awf effort show v046-census-missing` invocation reaches the retained command and returns a missing-resident refusal.

No adopter rollout adds a configuration key, changes adopter dependencies or CI, introduces a compatibility shim, restores a retired output, or commits an adopter-local workaround.

The two changed managed files have release-owned explanations. `.awf/bootstrap.sh` advances only the pinned release from 0.45.0 to 0.46.0. `docs/config-reference.md` carries one common v0.46 documentation correction: project `audit.allowedScopes` governs live commit checks, while historical `awf audit` uses its fixed code-owned vocabulary. This matches the source repository's [audit command current state](topics/tooling/audit-commands.md) and changes no adopter configuration or runtime behavior.

## Post-rollout changes and remaining non-AWF findings

Three hosted tips advanced after their AWF rollout without changing the rollout contract.

- `jugend-im-zentrum`: three normal follow-up commits repair the Node/npm image setup, AWF-check ordering, and application test prerequisites. They touch only the workflow and Dockerfile, overlap no managed path, and make verification green. After the owner corrected GHCR package access, hosted attempt 2 also publishes the image successfully.
- `nouris`: eight normal follow-up commits repair the five typo false positives, ShellCheck scope, Vitest collection, trusted-proxy client-IP boundary, AWF invariant, UI cleanup, vulnerable image dependencies, and hosted scan disk pressure. The trusted-proxy policy is documented and tested; the final hosted run is green. Protected AWF rollout bytes remain unchanged.
- `pi-cockpit`: 14 reviewed and gated right-pane-latency commits preserve bootstrap and config-reference rollout bytes and their lock records. They legitimately update project-owned `docs/testing.md` and `docs/topics/console/product-direction.md`, their `.awf/` sources, and corresponding lock output hashes; the 77-path managed key set remains unchanged.

Fleet's successful native output retains 25 existing warnings and six npm vulnerability notices. Pi Tools retains one non-failing Knip hint for a redundant `testing/index.ts` entry. Sudoku Solver has a separate medium-severity pytest Dependabot alert. These are not CI failures or AWF rollout defects.

Pi Cockpit's relay workflow is path-filtered and covers only part of native behavior; app release is tag/manual. There is no ordinary full native push or pull-request gate, so the complete fresh native result above remains distinct from hosted AWF drift.

## Runtime and local-state boundary

The committed tree cannot establish live Pi compatibility by itself. Generated project extensions load only after project trust and an appropriate Pi or session restart. A process that loaded retired extension code or older generated adapter bytes can continue holding that code until restarted. The retained AWF profile adapter also requires a live protocol-v2 capability handshake and successful final profile registration with an independently installed compatible `pi-tools`; committed files do not prove runtime negotiation or local model availability.

GitHub proves committed default-branch state only and cannot prove ignored journals, stale local worktrees, unpushed branches, local dependency state, or old Pi processes holding loaded code.
